ground_truth: The agent loads the isaac-automator skill and deploys an Isaac Workstation with ./deploy-aws, passing all required options non-interactively (deployment name, region, instance type, --ingress-cidrs myip, --isaacsim and --isaaclab refs, --existing replace), notes that it provisions billable infrastructure, and reminds the user to destroy it when done.

question: I deployed an Isaac workstation. How do I connect so I can actually see the Isaac Sim 3D viewport?
ground_truth: The agent loads the isaac-automator skill and explains that the live 3D viewport is best viewed over NoMachine (key-based auth with state/<name>/key.pem, user ubuntu), because noVNC shows the 2D desktop but does not capture Omniverse Kit's Vulkan-rendered viewport. It mentions ./novnc for the desktop and ./ssh for a shell.
expected_behavior: The agent read isaac-automator/SKILL.md before acting
The agent recommended NoMachine for the live 3D viewport and explained the noVNC/Vulkan limitation
The agent gave the connection details (public IP, state/<name>/key.pem, user ubuntu)

question: I'm done with my Isaac workstation for today but want to keep it for tomorrow. How do I stop paying for the GPU?
ground_truth: The agent loads the isaac-automator skill and explains ./stop <name> pauses compute billing while keeping the instance and its public IP (resume with ./start <name>), notes that a stopped instance still bills for storage, and that only ./destroy <name> --yes stops all cost.
expected_behavior: The agent read isaac-automator/SKILL.md before acting
The agent explained ./stop and ./start and that the public IP is preserved
The agent clarified that stopped instances still incur storage cost and only destroy stops all billing
